cards.text: Welcome in, friend. This book opens with the words of a man it calls the Teacher, a king in Jerusalem. And let me tell you, he does NOT ease into it.

cards.question: The Teacher, king in Jerusalem, is the son of ___.
Right away, the Teacher says only some things are futile.

cards.text: EVERYTHING, friend. He doesn't even say good morning. Just futility of futilities, TWICE, in case somebody in the back missed it, and then a question about all the labor a man toils at under the sun.

cards.question: The Teacher looks at all the labor a person toils at under the sun. What does he ask about it?

answers.text: What a man gains from it
How long a man must keep at it
Who a man is working for

cards.text: Then he zooms WAY out and looks at people across time. Generations come, and generations go.

cards.question: While the generations come and go, the Teacher says the ___ remains forever.
Then the Teacher points up: the sun rises and the sun sets. What does he say it does after it sets?

answers.text: Hurries back to where it rises

cards.text: It HURRIES back to do it all again. That's me hopping back to the oven before the last batch has even cooled.

cards.question: The Teacher watches the wind blow southward, then turn northward. What does he say it keeps doing?
All the rivers flow into the sea, and the Teacher says the sea finally fills up.
Once the streams reach the sea, where does the Teacher say they flow?

answers.text: Back to the place they came from

cards.text: Never full, and right back around again. That sea is me with a box of cookies, friend: you keep handing them over, I keep finding room.

cards.question: The Teacher says all things are wearisome, more than one can describe. He says the eye and the ear never get ___.

cards.text: NEVER enough. That's somebody on their phone at midnight: seen it all, STILL scrolling.

cards.question: The sun, the wind and the rivers all keep coming back around. So what does the Teacher say there is under the sun?

cards.text: Nothing new. So what about when somebody points at something and says, "Look, this is new"?

cards.question: Someone calls a thing brand new. What does the Teacher say about it?

answers.text: It came from a far country
It will not last a year

cards.text: Reminds me of the dead batteries I shared that drawer with. Same argument every single day, and every day they swore it was a brand new point.

cards.question: The Teacher also talks about being remembered. He says people yet to come will be remembered by those who follow after them.

findings.problem: This story card only restates the answer card 8 already gave (the sun hurries back) and adds a joke. It doesn't move the baker forward in the passage.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: This story card is only a joke about the drawer's batteries. It tells no part of the passage and moves nothing forward. The joke has no passage moment to ride along on.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The question says 'Once the streams reach the sea,' which adds a sequence the text doesn't state. Verse 1:7 only says 'to the place from which the streams come, there again they flow.' It never says this happens after the streams reach the sea.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The question begins 'The sun, the wind and the rivers all keep coming back around. So what does the Teacher say…' The 'So' presents verse 1:9 as a conclusion drawn from verses 5 to 7. The text doesn't state that connection.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Multiple choice makes up 6 of the stop's 12 choice cards. True or false and fill in the blank have only 3 each, so one type dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
